videoTitle: Josh McDowell: Manuscript Hunting and Mythmaking for Jesus

stratagems.name: Generalization
stratagems.description: Infers from documented narrative embellishment that McDowell's entire apologetic output is unreliable — eliding the distinction between personal testimony and the scholarly argument structure of ETDAV.

stratagems.name: Framing Through Loaded Metaphor
stratagems.description: Title uses 'mythmaking' — implying deliberate fabrication — where the evidence supports embellishment and reconstructive memory, not necessarily intentional deception.

stratagems.name: Appeal to Own Authority
stratagems.description: Repeatedly invokes his PhD, DSS specialty, and personal relationships with key figures as implicit warrants, functioning rhetorically to short-circuit scrutiny.

structuralVerdict.explanation: The core thesis — that McDowell progressively embellished his conversion-through-manuscript-research narrative — is well-documented across multiple editions of his own writings and is not refuted by any of the six false claims. However, Davis's conflation of two distinct 'first-century Mark' provenance chains (P137/EES vs. Carroll's 2013 event) introduces an unverified assertion that directly implicates McDowell's involvement and, if wrong, weakens the most damaging specific accusation in the video.

thesisCriticalErrors.description: The conflation of P137 with McDowell's 2013 discovery claim [Support] is the only false claim that directly implicates the thesis argument about McDowell's manuscript activities; the other five are factual imprecisions that do not affect the core embellishment narrative.

falseClaims.claim: The SWBTS fragment contained texts from Leviticus 21 that condemns homosexuality
falseClaims.notes: The relevant prohibitions are in Leviticus 18 and 20, not 21. Leviticus 21 addresses priestly physical disqualifications. The underlying argument is correct; only the chapter citation is wrong.

falseClaims.claim: Patterson solicited millions to acquire eight fragments for SWBTS
falseClaims.notes: SWBTS's own April 2020 statement describes six fragments purchased in two acquisitions in 2010. Eight were in negotiation but six were ultimately purchased.

falseClaims.claim: The supposed first-century Mark was 'a 3rd century fragment'
falseClaims.notes: P.Oxy. 5345 (P137) was dated 'late 2nd or earlier 3rd century CE' at publication. Calling it simply '3rd century' drops the early endpoint and overstates the distance from a first-century claim.

falseClaims.claim: This was the same fragment that McDowell had claimed to discover in his 2013 talk
falseClaims.notes: Davis conflates P137 (from the EES Oxyrhynchus collection, shown by Obbink in 2011) with Carroll's mask-dismounting at McDowell's December 2013 event. No direct evidence links these two distinct provenance chains.

falseClaims.claim: Sean McDowell is 'an assistant professor in the Christian apologetics program at Biola University'
falseClaims.notes: By 2023 Biola identifies Sean McDowell as Associate Professor at Talbot School of Theology. May have been accurate at production but imprecise at publication.

falseClaims.claim: The Baylor 2012 event 'was itself a hoax at which no new discoveries were actually made'
falseClaims.notes: 'Hoax' implies intentional deception of the audience, which Davis does not demonstrate. The accurate characterization is that no discoveries were made and the event was theatrically staged.
